lines.t: You said, “I kept the rules, I gave when asked, and sang the songs.”
You said your hands were clean, your house in order - why must I be so hard?
I heard the words you wore like robes, the tidy prayers you gave,
I watched the lamps you trimmed, felt seats you warmed with faith.
Yet this Word I set before you is a plumb line, straight and true,
My alarm to wake the sleeper, and correction when due.
I do not hunger for your show; I hunger for a willing heart.
I ask for all. not scraps. give me your hands, and do not keep Me apart.
My arms are open but you keep Me at arms length.
This call is for the humble who answer without restraint.
Give directly to the poor; when asked, give drink and cloak and bread.
Tithe not just coin but strength and time - lay down the comforts that you’ve led.
Walk the path of sacrifice; this is the way My people prove,
Not public praise no simple sermons, but yield and in Me, move.
You say, “Why, Lord? Must I lose the things I hold so tight?”
My Child, I prune to bring forth fruit; let go, beloved, take flight.
Pour out all that you would not give;
Lay yourself upon My stone and truly live.”
The least among you hear and run - the poor, the meek, the one who’s bare;
The widow, thief in sorrow, lame and weary. My table waits for all who cares.
Come out before the time; be plucked up, escape what must soon take place.
I do not hunger for your show; I hunger for a willing heart.
I ask for all. not scraps. Give me your hands, and do not keep Me apart.
My arms are open but you keep Me at arms length.
This call is for the humble who answer without restraint.

I weep; yet I call; my heart is not glad at hardened stone.
If you will come, you will be found; if not, the door must close.
Harden not your heart; come out and find your rest.
The fields are white, the harvest waits; He with ears to hear, hear Me!

I surrendered all to you in My passion!
